name: Ken Griffin
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2008-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2021); Hurun Unicorn founders (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Ken Griffin founded and runs Citadel, a Miami-based hedge fund firm that manages $68 billion in assets.
Griffin founded Citadel in 1990 but first began trading from his Harvard dorm in 1987. He put a satellite dish on the roof to get real-time stock quotes.
Citadel is the world's most profitable hedge fund and has generated $83 billion in net gains since inception in 1990, according to LCH Investments.
Citadel Securities, one of Wall Street's biggest market-making firms, is responsible for one of every four stock trades in the U.S.
Griffin has given some $2.4 billion to philanthropic causes. Recent beneficiaries include Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center and nonprofit hospitals in Miami.
forbes_facts: Griffin bought rare editions of the Emancipation Proclamation and the Thirteenth Amendment, signed by Abraham Lincoln, to be loaned for public display in 2025.
Griffin's first job was selling Franklin Mint collectibles.

name: Sunil Mittal
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2004-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun India (2015-2022)
forbes_bio: Telecom tycoon Sunil Mittal's Bharti Airtel is among India's largest mobile phone operators. It has more than 600 million customers across South Asia and Africa.
Airtel, which has SingTel as its partner, competes with Mukesh Ambani's Reliance Jio and Kumar Birla's Vodafone Idea.
In 2022, Google announced a $1 billion investment in Bharti Airtel,of which $700 million was for a minority stake in the company.
Mittal's Bharti Global, run by his son Shravin, has stakes in France's Eutelsat, and U.K. telecoms giant BT Group, where Mittal has a board seat.
forbes_facts: Bharti was set up in 1976 as a maker of bicycle parts.
Mittal and his two siblings have pledged $1.1 billion to their charitable foundation, mainly to set up a new university to provide free education for the poor.
Mittal has been conferred the Padma Bhushan, one of India's highest civilian awards.
In March 2024, Indian-American billionaire investor Rajiv Jain's GQG Partners bought a $713 million stake in Bharti Airtel from SingTel.

name: Tilman Fertitta
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2012-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Serving as President Trump's ambassador to Italy "is a real job," says Fertitta, who personally oversaw the renovation of Villa Taverna, the ambassador's residence in Rome.
Fertitta also owns the Golden Nugget Casinos and Landry's, a Texas-based restaurant and entertainment company.
Landry's brands include Landry's Seafood House, Bubba Gump Shrimp Co. and Saltgrass Steak House.
Fertitta took Landry's private in 2010 in a deal worth $1.4 billion.
In September 2025 Fertitta put his 275-foot yacht Boardwalk up for sale for about $175 million. He has a bigger one on order.
forbes_facts: Fertitta first learned the food business at his father's seafood restaurant where he worked after school.
He bought land on the Vegas Strip for $270 million, but Fertitta put plans for a megacasino on hold after acquiring a large stake in Wynn Resorts.

name: Andreas Struengmann
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2012-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: Andreas Struengmann and twin brother Thomas were early backers of BioNTech, which partnered with Pfizer to make a vaccine for Covid-19.
The brothers cofounded generic drugmaker Hexal in 1986 and sold it to Novartis in 2005 for some $7 billion.
The brothers invest in biotech, pharma, life sciences and healthcare companies through their Zug, Switzerland-based investment firm, Santo Holding.
In 2008, they established a neuroscience research center in Frankfurt named after their father, Ernst Struengmann.
forbes_facts: After studying medicine in Freiburg, Germany, Andreas worked as a doctor in South Africa.

name: Todd Boehly
sec_insider_companies: LSB INDUSTRIES, INC. (LXU) - TenPercentOwner; Vivid Seats Inc. (SEAT) - Director,TenPercentOwner; Kennedy-Wilson Holdings, Inc. (KW) - Director
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2022-2025); Hurun Global (2023-2026); Wikidata (2025); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Todd Boehly cofounded holding company Eldridge Industries in 2015, after building Guggenheim Partners' credit business and serving as president.
The company acquired some of his first assets from Guggenheim, including insurer Security Benefit, which provides deal financing to this day.
Eldridge Industries has grown into a diverse conglomerate with investments ranging from Bruce Springsteen's song rights to daily fantasy and sports-betting firm DraftKings.
Boehly personally holds minority stakes in the Los Angeles Lakers and Los Angeles Dodgers (Eldridge has a separate minority stake in the latter).
A group led by Boehly reached a record deal to buy soccer team Chelsea FC from Russian owner Roman Abramovich for $3.1 billion in 2022.
forbes_facts: Boehly and his wife Katie, who met at Wiliam and Mary, gave an undisclosed sum to the college to build the Boehly Center for Excellence in Finance.
Boehly slept on a park bench in Kansas while scouting Security Benefit for Guggenheim, because his hotel room smelled like cigarettes.

name: Anthony Bamford
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (1997-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Anthony Bamford and his family own JCB, a construction equipment manufacturer that does nearly $7 billion in annual revenue.
Bamford's father launched JCB in a garage in Uttoxeter, England, in 1945.
JCB sells products in 150 countries. Customers include the U.S. military.
forbes_facts: The brand is so ingrained in British culture that a JCB is to a backhoe what a Kleenex is to a tissue.
Bamford, who joined the House of Lords in 2013, was a vocal Brexit supporter.

name: Blair Parry-Okeden
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2008-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2025)
forbes_bio: Blair Parry-Okeden inherited a 25% stake in Cox Enterprises in 2007 when her mother, Barbara Cox Anthony, passed away.
Cox Enterprises is a billion dollar (sales) communications, automotive and media company based in Atlanta; it owns cable TV firm Cox Communications.
Blair's brother, Jim Kennedy, is chairman emeritus of the company.
Her grandfather, James M. Cox, founded the company in 1898 with the purchase of the Dayton Evening News newspaper.
forbes_facts: Blair Parry-Okeden grew up in Hawaii and now lives quietly in Australia. She has no role at the company.
She is a former teacher and wrote a children's book, Down By The Gate, in 1989.

name: Robert Ng
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (1996-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Robert Ng and his brother Philip control Far East Organization, Singapore's largest private landlord and property developer.
The group was founded by their father Ng Teng Fong, who moved from China to Singapore in 1934 and came to be known as "The King of Orchard Road."
Their Hong Kong arm, Sino Group, is run by older sibling Robert's son Daryl, while Philip oversees the Singapore interests.
Singapore-listed Far East Orchard repurposed the century-old former Westminster Fire Station in London into a luxury development with 17 apartments and put it on sale in 2022.
forbes_facts: The brothers are staunch Christians and refer to Far East as a Christian enterprise.
Founder Ng Teng Fong spurned his family's grocery store and got into real estate in 1960 against his father's wishes.

name: Franz von Baumbach
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Franz von Baumbach is an heir to the Boehringer Ingelheim fortune, a company best known as the largest private player in the pharmaceutical industry.
Founded in 1885, the company grew by making ingredients for pharmacies, textile merchants and the food industry; and boasted a workforce of 1,500 by 1939.
Today, Boehringer Ingelheim, whose most well-known drugs treat COPD, anti-coagulation and type 2 diabetes, employs 53,000 people and has a presence in 130 markets.

He began buying land outside of Marbella in the 1990s and built his first shopping mall, Parque Comercial La Canada, on that land.

name: Vlad Tenev
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026); Hurun Global U40 (2026); Wikidata (2025); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2026)
forbes_bio: Vlad Tenev is CEO of stock trading app Robinhood Markets, which he founded in 2013 with his friend Baiju Bhatt.
Since its launch, Robinhood's no-commission trading model has revolutionized the brokerage industry.
In 2021, Robinhood went public on the Nasdaq exchange at a $32 billion valuation.
Tenev owns more than 6% of the company.
The son of two World Bank staffers, Tenev was born in Bulgaria and grew up in Washington, D.C.
forbes_facts: In December 2020, Robinhood agreed to pay $65 million to the Securities and Exchange Commission to settle charges of deceiving customers about its revenue sources.
Tenev met his cofounder Baiju Bhatt while the two were undergraduates at Stanford University.
